How Far Above Its Mode the Inner Fit Stopped

Source: R/outer_context.R
inner_mode_error.Rd

Returns \(\tfrac12 g'K^{-1}g\), the decrease that the penalized likelihood's own Newton correction predicts at the point that the inner fit returned, which is the amount of log-likelihood still to be gained there.

Usage

inner_mode_error(ctx, spec, design, coef, hyper, score, expected = FALSE)

Arguments

ctx

The evaluation context, so the penalized factorization is the one that the criterion will read rather than a second copy.

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

coef

The coefficients that the inner fit returned.

hyper

The hyperparameters.

score

The inner objective's gradient at those coefficients.

expected

Whether the penalized information is the expected one.

Value

A single number, or NA where the penalized system could not be read there, which is itself a reason to call the point unavailable.

Details

Its value determines whether a point is available. The inner optimizer's flag concerns a different question: it reports whether a stopping rule fired. Availability is whether the criterion, a Laplace expansion at the mode, is valid at this point.

Availability is a matter of distance and has a natural scale, log-likelihood units. The flag is a boolean about a threshold on a score whose size depends on the model. The two can differ: an inner fit may stop on the objective-stall guard while the score is slightly above the absolute tolerance and the penalized likelihood is already at its mode to many digits. Such a point is available by this reading and unavailable by the flag.

It is used to add points and not to remove any: a run whose flag reports convergence stays usable whatever this reads.

See also

mode_error_limit(), criterion_resolution()
